items.e: In the name of the one who speaks righteousness and declares things that are right I will explain the Torah portion which begins with These Are The Words . Some say that the meaning of eleven days’ journey from Horeb…by the way of mount Seir (v. 2) is: Look. They traveled for forty years in the wilderness. This is the meaning of And it came to pass in the fortieth year (v. 3). However, they err, for Israel came up to Kadesh-barnea in the second year. Actually, And it came to pass in the fortieth year is connected to that Moses spoke (v. 3). I believe that These are the words (v. 1) refers to the precepts recorded in the Torah portions Re’ah Anokhi , Shoftim , Ki Tetze , and Ve-hayah Ki Tavo , which were already spoken by Moses when they were in the wilderness. Moses spoke (v. 1) should be read as if written twice. This means Moses spoke, in the wilderness, in the Arabah, and in Suph from the day that they journeyed from Sinai.

BETWEEN PARAN AND TOPHEL, AND LABAN, AND HAZEROTH, AND DI-ZAHAB. Places not mentioned in the Torah portion These Are the Stages (Num. 33:1). On the other hand, they might have been mentioned under other names, for, observe, Senir has three names. There are many other such instances.

IT IS ELEVEN DAYS’ JOURNEY. This means that Moses spoke these things in those eleven days. FROM HOREB. That they went from Horeb to Kadeshbarnea. I have already told you that the spies went out from Kadesh-barnea. After God swore that they would not enter the land, no new commandment was given to them. No new commandment was revealed until the fortieth year. We find the aforementioned to be so. Took Moses upon him to expound this law (v. 5) is proof of this. Moses expounded the laws which he had stated between Paran and Tophel, for most of the commandments are in this book. According unto all that the Lord had given him in commandment unto them (v. 3), refers to the precepts given beyond the Jordan; in the wilderness, in the Arabah (v. 1). If you understand the secret of the twelve and also that of So Moses wrote (Deut. 31:22); And the Canaanite was then in the Land (Gen. 12:6); In the mount where the Lord is seen (Gen. 22:14); and behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron (Deut. 3:11); then you will recognize the truth.

Some say that Moses died on the first day of Shevat. Scripture states that Israel mourned thirty days (Deut. 34:8). They spent six Sabbaths there. They offer proof from that selfsame day (Deut. 32:48), i.e., that Moses read this book before all of Israel in one day and then died on that very day. However, this is no proof, for that selfsame day refers to the song. Look! Scripture states, thou art to pass over the Jordan this day (Deut. 9:1).
IN THE ELEVENTH MONTH. I have explained the meaning of ashte asar (eleven) in my comments on the Torah portion Nasso .

TOOK MOSES UPON HIM TO EXPLAIN. Ho’il (took upon himself) and be’er (to explain) are two verbs in the perfect attached to each other without a connective vav . We find the same in chamak avar (had turned away, and was gone) (Cant. 5:6). Look! Moses began to explain to the children who were born in the wilderness what happened to their fathers. He related to them all the commandments. They would also hear from the mouth of the faithful messenger the Ten Statements which their fathers heard from God.
HOREB. This is Sinai, as I have previously noted.
TURN YOU. Leave this place. AND TAKE YOUR JOURNEY. It is the style of Scripture to say, u-se’u lakhem (and take your journey). Compare, lekh lekha (get thee out) (Gen.2:1).
I AM NOT ABLE TO BEAR YOU MYSELF ALONE. Its meaning is similar to thou art not able to perform it alone (Ex. 18:18).
HATH MULTIPLIED YOU. In Egypt, and the blessing which your father blessed you was fulfilled.
[AS THE STARS OF HEAVEN.] This is a metaphor.
A THOUSAND TIMES. The word pe’amim (times) comes with elef (a thousand) and with me’ah (a hundred). The reverse is the case in Arabic.
YOUR CUMBRANCE. Torchakhem (your cumbrance) is related to the word torach (burden) in They are a burden unto me (Is. 1:14). Your cumbrance refers to teaching the commandments to the simple.
AND YOUR BURDEN. They demanded bread, water, and meat. Compare, that Thou layest the burden of all this people upon me (Num. 11:11).
AND YOUR STRIFE. One with another.
GET YOU. The word havu (get) is irregular. Its heh should have been vocalized with a sheva na and a pattach .
AND FULL OF KNOWLEDGE. Men who were known, men whom all recognized.
CAPTAINS OF THOUSANDS. I have already explained this.

HEAR. Shamo’a (hear) is an infinitive. It is like the word zakhor (remember) in Remember the sabbath day (Ex. 20:8). Shamo’a is short for shamo’a shimu (you shall surely hear) or shimu shamo’a (you shall surely hear).
THE STRANGER THAT IS WITH HIM. I have already explained the meaning of the term ger (stranger).
RESPECT PERSONS IN JUDGMENT. To force judgment in favor of the person whom he [the judge] recognizes.
WHICH YE SHOULD DO. The reference is to the statutes and laws which he [Moses] taught them.
ALL THAT GREAT AND DREADFUL WILDERNESS. This is what the eleven day’s journey (v. 2) refers to.

[THE HILL-COUNTRY OF THE AMORITES.] For Scripture states, [ And the Amorites, that dwell in that hill-country, came out against you… ] and beat you down in Seir, even unto Hormah (Deut. 1:44). This means that we should go out toward the hill country of the Amorites.
TAKE POSSESSION. Resh (take possession) is vocalized like the word shev (sit). Resh is related to the word yerushah (possession).
DISMAYED. Techat (dismayed) is similar to the word yiddal (shall be made thin) in That the glory of Jacob shall be made thin (Is. 17:4). Techat comes from a double root.

THAT THEY MAY SEARCH THE LAND FOR US. Veyachperu (that they may search) is similar to la-chepo r (to search out) in to search out all the land (Josh. 2:3). One who digs ( chofer ) searches for that which is hidden.
BY WHICH WE MUST GO UP. At first.
AND THE THING PLEASED ME WELL. Because you all assented to this.
AND BROUGHT IT DOWN. Moses said this because of the height of the tree. Actually, however, he said this because they were in the south.

AND YE MURMURED. Va-teragenu (and ye murmured) is similar to rogenim (murmur) in And they that murmur shall learn instruction (Is. 29:24). Teragenu (murmured) is in the nifal . Compare, al te’atzevu (be not grieved).
DREAD NOT. Lo ta’artzun means dread not. Ta’artzun is related to the word ma’aritzekhem (your dread) in and let him be your dread (Is. 8:13). It means the breaking of the heart by fear.
HE SHALL FIGHT FOR YOU. Lakhem means for you.
TO PITCH YOUR TENTS. La-chanotekhem (to pitch your tents) is not a transitive verb, for we do not find this form to be transitive.
TO SHOW YOU. La-re’otekhem (to show you) is vocalized with a pattach to show that the letter heh , which is placed before the direct object ( le-hare’otekhem ) is missing.
SAVE. The yod in zulati (save) is superfluous, for the word is found without the yod .
AND TO HIM WILL I GIVE THE LAND THAT HE HATH TRODDEN UPON. The reference is to Hebron.

[ALSO THE LORD WAS ANGRY WITH ME.] I have already shown you that the nun of the word appo (his anger) (Gen. 39:19) is swallowed by the peh . However, it is present in the Aramaic. Furthermore, appo is also related to the word anafta (thou was angry) in For though Thou was angry with me (Is. 12:1) and hitannaf (was angry) in Also the Lord was angry with me . Moses mentions Caleb first, then Joshua. I have already explained why.
WHO STANDETH BEFORE THEE. This is his minister (Ex. 24:13; Num. 11:28).
THAT THIS DAY HAVE NO KNOWLEDGE. That day.
OF GOOD OR EVIL. Scripture speaks of the majority.

AND DEEMED IT A LIGHT THING. The meaning of va-tahinu (and deemed it a light thing) is, and you said behold ( hen ). Do not ask how a verb can be derived from a word that is connected to another word, for we find the same with al . The same is true, as I have explained, of the word pen (lest), for we find the word afunah (I am distracted) (Ps. 88:16). Others say that va-tahinu is related to the word hin . Its meaning is a measure. However, this is far-fetched.
AND THE AMORITES…CAME OUT. The reference, as I have explained, is to the Canaanites.
AS BEES DO. For they immediately chase after and bite whoever touches their abode.
AND BEAT YOU DOWN. I have explained the meaning of va-yakketu (and beat you down). It is related to the word ve-khatoti (and I will beat to pieces) (Ps. 99:24).
UNTO HORMAH. Hormah is either the name of a place or an infinitive.
SO YE ABODE IN KADESH. Kadesh-barnea.

MANY DAYS, ACCORDING UNTO THE DAYS THAT YE ABODE THERE. In spying out the land. If one should argue, the spies alone abode there. [The answer is:] Scripture similarly reads, After the number of days in which ye spied out the land (Num. 14:34).
CONTEND NOT WITH THEM. The word titgaru (contend) is similar to the word yigareh (strife) in stirreth up strife (Prov. 28:25). It means to disturb and err.

YE SHALL PURCHASE FOOD OF THEM. If they want to sell. Some say that our clause is to be read as a question. It means that Israel had no need for food and drink in these past years. For the Lord thy God hath blessed thee (v. 7) is proof.
I HAVE GIVEN AR. Of Moab. It is possible that Sihon took Ar and that it returned to Maob at the end.
THE EMIM. I have previously explained the meaning of Emim. Scripture tells us that Moab took Ar from the Emim.
REPHAIM. I have previously explained its meaning.
THE HORITES. They are the sons of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:20).
TO DISCOMFIT THEM. Le-hummam (to discomfit them) is a kal . It comes from a double root.

SO IT CAME TO PASS, WHEN ALL THE MEN OF WAR WERE CONSUMED. Our verse is connected to that the Lord spoke unto me saying (v. 17). It is similar to And it came to pass, when Moses had made an end of writing (Deut. 31:24) and And it came to pass on the day when the Lord spoke (Ex. 6:28). There are many other such cases. It means, And it came to pass when they were consumed, God said that we are about to pass over the border of Ar.
AND WHEN THOU COMEST NIGH OVER AGAINST THE CHILDREN OF AMMON. The meaning of ve-karavta is, when you come close to them.
HARASS THEM NOT. Tetzurem (harass) comes from a double root.
NOR CONTEND WITH THEM. Titgar (contend) is in the hitpa’el . Its root ends in a heh .
ZAMZUMMIM. A foreign term which was Hebraized. Compare, ha-achashdarpenim (the satraps) (Esth. 8:9).
BUT THE LORD DESTROYED THEM. Scripture relates that God destroyed a people on behalf of the Moabites and gave them the land as an inheritance, as he did with Mount Seir on behalf of Esau.

[AS FAR AS GAZA.] Scripture reads as far as Gaza because Gaza belonged to the Philistines and there already was a covenant between Abraham and Abimelech, namely, that thou wilt not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son (Gen. 21:23). Scripture relates that the Avvim took Gaza.
BEGIN TO POSSESS IT. The word rash (possess) comes from the word yerushah (possession).
OUT OF THE WILDERNESS OF KEDEMOTH. I believe that the wilderness of Kedemoth is the same as the place called the wilderness to Mattanah (Num. 21:18).
THE HIGHWAY. The well-known highway.
THOU SHALT SELL ME FOOD FOR MONEY, THAT I MAY EAT. If I need to.

AS THE CHILDREN OF ESAU…AND THE MOABITES THAT DWELL IN AR DID UNTO ME. Some say that did unto me refers to thou shalt sell me food for money . If this is so, then what will they do with the inhabitants of Ar who were Moabites, about whom Scripture writes, because they met you not with bread and with water in the way (Deut. 23:5)? They were compelled to offer this interpretation because the king of the Edomites said, Thou shalt not pass through me (Ex. 20:18). I believe that Israel’s request refers to, I will go along by the highway (v. 27) as the children of Esau did, for Israel went around Mount Seir by the highway. Indeed, Scripture reads, Ye are to pass through the border of your brethren the children of Esau, that dwell in Seir (v. 4). However, the king, that is, the king of Edom, did not allow them to pass through his country, which was near Canaan. Israel therefore passed by Ar, as Scripture records (v. 18). Others say that they did not meet the Israelites but the Israelites bought from them.

I HAVE BEGUN. The heh of hachilloti (I have begun), which is the heh of the form, is vocalized with a pattach because of the guttural. Compare, ha’irotihu (roused him) in I have roused him up in victory (Is. 45:13).
AND WE SMOTE. The root nun is missing in the word va-nakh (and we smote).
THE MEN. Metim (men) means people.
TOO HIGH. Sagevah (too high) is related to the word venisgav (shall be exalted) in And the Lord alone shall be exalted (Is. 2:11).
TO THE LAND OF THE CHILDREN OF AMMON. Which, as I have noted, is today in their hands.
ALL THE SIDE. The word yad (side) means place. Compare, yad (side) in by the side of the Jordan (Num. 13:29).
NONE WAS LEFT TO HIM. Each of the Israelites [left none to him]. Hishir is in the perfect.

THE REGION OF ARGOB. The words of the Aramaic translator are known. Some say that Argob is the name of a person who possessed this region as an inheritance from his father. Some go far afield and say that the alef of Argob is superfluous and that Argob is related to the word regavim (clods) in And the clods cleave fast together (Job 38:38).

AFTER THE CUBIT OF A MAN. After the cubit of a normal person. Observe, Og was double in size. It is unlikely that the Torah is speaking of Og’s cubit, for if this were so, then what is Scripture trying to teach? Furthermore, he would not have the image of a person at all.
JAIR THE SON OF MANASSEH. I have already explained that he came from the tribe of Judah.
THE GESHURITES AND THE MAACATHITES. Two nations.
TO MACHIR. This was explained.
THE MIDDLE OF THE VALLEY FOR A BORDER. The word u-gevul (for a border) is be rendered, and its border. So too u-gevul (the border thereof) in the Jordan being the border thereof (v. 17).

AND I COMMANDED YOU. Moses speaks to the children of Gad and Reuben. He uses the term you, not them, because they are included among the Israelites. The reverse is true with, that Moses commanded the Levites…Take this book of the law…For I know thy rebellion (Deut. 31:25-27). Moses did not address the Levites. On the contrary, he spoke to all of Israel. He addressed the Levites because they are included in all of Israel.

The meaning of va-etchannan (and I besought) is, and I had already besought . When Moses mentioned Joshua and said, And I commanded Joshua , etc. (v. 21) because I am not passing over with you, he had already asked the Lord to be allowed to pass over with the Israelites; for God’s greatness is unsearchable (Ps. 145:3) and They are new every morning; Great is Thy faithfulness (Lam. 3:23).
THOU HAST BEGUN. The wisest of the wise said: Thou hast begun to show Thy servant Thy greatness , in heaven and on earth, i.e., the manner in which You conduct the world.

AND THY STRONG HAND. Via the signs performed through Moses so that the world learned that there is no God but the Lord. The meaning of El (God) is mighty. IN HEAVEN. Wherein are the angels and the hosts. OR ON EARTH. Wherein are the beasts and human beings.
ACCORDING TO THY WORKS. All of which are governed by wisdom.
MIGHTY. In ability. This section was written to instill a love of the Land of Israel. If they love the land, they will observe God’s commandments so that they will not be exiled from the land.
GET THEE UP INTO THE TOP OF PISGAH. The reference is to the valley that is in the field of Moab, the top of Pisgah.

SO WE ABODE IN THE VALLEY. The meaning is, and we had already stayed in this valley, which is the top of Pisgah, for from there they journeyed to the plains of Moab. The valley is in the mountains of Abarim, for the latter is clearly stated. Moses now commenced to speak about the commandments. He began with idol worship because they were near Bethpeor.
WHICH I TEACH YOU, TO DO THEM. The main purpose of study is the observance of the commandments.
THAT YE MAY LIVE. For those who worshipped pe’or were destroyed.

AND POSSESS. The middle root letter of the verb vi-yerishtem (and possess) is vocalized with a chirik because the yod is silenced and made invisible by the chirik beneath the vav . There is no other word that is similarly vocalized.

YE SHALL NOT ADD. On your own and think that it is in the service of God. You shall similarly not diminish. Now, my statement that ye may live does not require witnesses, for Your eyes have seen… (v. 3).
IN BAAL-PEOR. Be-va’al pe’or (in Baal-peor) means because of Baal-peor. There are many such instances. Whoever did not worship Baal-peor is alive.

[I HAVE TAUGHT YOU.] Moses states, I have taught you , after saying which I teach you (v. 1), because he wants to add, even as the Lord my God commanded me . The meaning of our verse is, the precepts which I taught you are God’s commandments, which you should observe in the land that God will give you for a possession. Furthermore, the commandments are your glory over the nations. 6. YOUR WISDOM AND YOUR UNDERSTANDING IN THE SIGHT OF THE PEOPLES. Because an intelligent person can understand the basis of all the commandments. An intelligent person can ascertain the reason why they were given.

FOR WHAT GREAT NATION IS THERE. That has God so near in that He always answers him in all that he intelligently requests of Him. Furthermore, unlike Israel there is no great nation that has statutes and ordinances that reason tells us are righteous.
A great nation means, great in intelligent people who fear the Lord.
ONLY TAKE HEED TO THYSELF. Its meaning is, should you forget everything, do not forget the day that you stood at Sinai.
WHICH THINE EYES SAW. The reference is to And all the people perceived the thunderings, and the lightnings (Ex. 20:15).
[ALL THE DAYS THAT THEY LIVE UPON THE EARTH.] Scripture says this because God knows that they can not properly observe His commandments when they are in countries where others rule over them.
UNTO THE HEART OF HEAVEN. The middle of heaven. Scripture speaks of those who look up. The heart of the sea (Ex. 15:8) is similar.
ONLY A VOICE. Which you heard, for the voice is not visible to the eye. I have already explained the meaning of And all the people saw the sounds (Ex. 20:15).

[COMMANDED ME AT THAT TIME.] For God told Moses all the statutes and ordinances at Sinai. However, Moses related them to Israel in the second year and again in the fortieth year. [Moses tells the Israelites:] Since you saw no form (v. 12) take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves (v. 15) lest you corrapt what you saw (v. 16), that is, lest you corrupt the truth or your ways.
A GRAVEN IMAGE. The word pesel (graven image) refers to an object that has been fashioned. Compare, va-yifselu (did fashion) in And Solomon’s builders…did fashion them (I Kings 5:32).

MALE OR FEMALE. Worshipped by some well-known nations. There are also nations that bow down and worship any beast that they meet at the beginning of their day in order to bring down a power from on high; for example, they worship the scorpion if they want someone bitten. The same applies to the remaining forty-seven forms.

THE SUN AND THE MOON. Which are the great lights. After mentioning the stars, Scripture goes on to use a general term, namely, even all the host of heaven. All the hosts of heaven refers to the planets, which are light-giving stars, and all the constellations and forms.
THOU BE DRAWN AWAY. You will, as it were, slip and fall.

WHICH THE LORD THY GOD HATH ALLOTTED. It has been empirically established that each and every nation has a specific star and constellation. Every city similarly has its own constellation. God raised Israel to a very high level in that God, and not any star, is Israel’s guide. Israel is thus God’s portion.

[NOW THE LORD WAS ANGERED WITH ME.] Moses says this because he had stated earlier, But you hath the Lord taken and brought forth…to be unto Him a people of inheritance (v. 20) in the land, so that you will serve Him. However, I will not share in this good.
FOR YOUR SAKES. You were the cause of my not entering the land. I have already explained this.

TAKE HEED UNTO YOURSELVES…AND MAKE YOU A GRAVEN IMAGE. Moses had previously said something to this effect. He repeated himself because he wanted to add, For the Lord thy God is a devouring fire (v. 24). Hence I command you to [ take heed unto yourselves …].
EVEN THE LIKENESS OF ANY THING. Temunat kol is to be rendered as the likeness of anything.

WHICH THE LORD THY GOD HATH FORBIDDEN THEE. Asher tzivvekha (hath forbidden thee) is to be rendered as He commanded thee. Or tzivvekha may be interpreted: which He commanded you not to make. Compare, I will also command (atzavveh) the clouds (from raining rain upon it) (Is. 5:6). Some say that the reference is to the likeness of the stars. However, this appears to me to be far-fetched.
A DEVOURING FIRE. There is no kaf with the meaning of like prefixed to the word esh (fire). The meaning of esh okhlah hu (a devouring fire) is, like a devouring fire.
A JEALOUS GOD. With regard to idol worship. His jealousy devours like fire, which does not leave root or branch.
WHEN THOU SHALT BEGET CHILDREN. Moses first tells the Israelites that the Lord God is a jealous God. He then tells them what will happen to them if they make an image.
AND YOU SHALL DEAL CORRUPTLY. With regard to the rest of the commandments such as to murder or to commit adultery.

I CALL HEAVEN AND EARTH TO WITNESS AGAINST YOU THIS DAY. Some say the witness of heaven and earth refers to the angels and the human beings. Others say that the reference is to the rain, as in and I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass (Lev. 26:19). However, it appears to me that heaven and earth are witnesses, and the Israelites and their children will always see them, for they are everlasting, as in as the days of the heavens above the earth (Deut. 11:21). Hear, O ye mountains, the Lord’s controversy (Micah 6:2); and Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us (Josh. 24:27) are similar. Should one dispute this on the basis of For the heavens shall vanish like smoke (Is. 51:6) and the like, [then I respond] the one who makes this argument is awake but his heart sleeps.
YE SHALL SOON UTTERLY PERISH. The word tovedun (ye shall utterly perish) is similar to tilmedun (that you may teach). The word is so vocalized because it is not in the construct.
FEW IN NUMBER. I have already explained the meaning of mete (few).

WHICH NEITHER SEE, NOR HEAR. Scripture mentions the four senses. It is unnecessary to mention the fifth because it is thicker than the others. Furthermore, it is the root of the life of the body. Do not be amazed at the terms u-vikashtem (but…ye will seek) and u-matzata (and thou shalt find) for Scripture speaks to many, to an entire nation, or to one person.
WITH ALL THY HEART. I will explain this later.
HE WILL NOT FAIL THEE. Yarpekha (fail thee) is the opposite of strengthen thee.
FOR ASK NOW OF THE DAYS PAST. She’al na means ask now.
SINCE THE DAY. The lamed of le-min (since) is superfluous. There are many such examples. On the other hand, it may be there for literary purposes.
AND FROM THE ONE END OF HEAVEN. Heaven, as I have explained, refers to the air, which has ends.
WHETHER THERE HATH BEEN. In his days.
OR HATH BEEN HEARD LIKE IT. The reference being to Did ever a people hear… (v. 33).
OR HATH GOD ASSAYED. Some say that Elohim (God) does not refer to the Lord. Heaven forbid. It most certainly refers to God.
ASSAYED. Scripture employs human language so that those who hear will understand.
BY TRIALS. This is a general term. Or it refers to trials done via signs. Compare, and did the signs in the sight of the people (Ex. 4:30).
AND BY WONDERS. The ten plagues. Scripture states, and Moses and Aaron did all these wonders (Ex. 11:10).
AND BY WAR. The reference is most probably to the killing of the first-born and to the punishments meted out to the gods of Egypt.
AND BY A MIGHTY HAND. The reference is to Israel’s departure by high hand. The outstretched arm refers to the pillar of fire and the pillar of cloud.
AND BY GREAT TERRORS. The drowning of Pharaoh and his army along with the splitting of the sea on behalf of Israel.
IN EGYPT. To the people of Egypt.
IT WAS SHOWN. Horeta (it was shown) is a hofal . The meaning of our clause is, God showed you all this so that you will know that He alone is God.

[THERE IS NONE ELSE.] This is to be understood according to the hint which I gave in my commentary on Koheleth on the verse that reads, for one higher than the high (Eccles. 5:7). Hence Scripture reads, There is none else .

[GOD.] I have explained the meaning of Elohim (God) in the Torah portion And Jethro Heard . Scripture states, And God (Elohim) spoke (Ex. 20:1); and God (Elohim) answered him by a voice (Ex. 19:19); God (Elohim) is come (Ex. 20:17); where God (Elohim) was (Ex. 20:18); for Elohim (God) was the speaker. [I quoted these verses] because there are some who do not understand when one is being brief. It is a deep secret.

THAT HE MIGHT INSTRUCT THEE. He made thee to hear Him so that you would fear Him. This is borne out when Israel said, but let not God speak with us, lest we die (Ex. 20:16). Look, you feared because of what your eyes saw and your ears heard. There was another reason why God made you hear His voice. He did so because He loved your fathers (v. 37), your fathers being three.
AND CHOSE THEIR SEED. Be-zaro (their seed) alludes to Jacob. If Scripture had read be-zaram (their seed), then the eight nations would have been included with us.

AND BROUGHT THEE OUT WITH HIS PRESENCE. Befanav (with His presence) means with His anger. He was angry at Egypt. Others say that panav (presence) here is similar to panav (presence) in And the angel of His presence saved them (Is. 63:9). However, I believe that panav (presence) here is similar to panekha (thine own person) in and thou go to battle in thy own person (Josh. 17:11).

AS IT IS THIS DAY. Close to this day. However, it really alludes to their possession of the land of the two Amorite kings, for Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh are called Israel. Scripture similarly reads, as Israel did unto the land of his possession (Deut. 2:12). The reference is not to the future, as many explain. Proof of the latter is the fact that the psalm which opens with the words, O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good (Ps. 136) reads, To Him that smote great kings (Ps. 136:17). Now the psalm only mentions Sihon and Og (Ps. 136:19,20). The psalm says, And gave their land for a heritage…Even a heritage unto Israel (Ps. 136:21,22). After stating that the Lord, He is God; there is none else beside Him (v. 35), Moses explains why by giving a very valuable reason. He begins with what the eye sees and goes on to logic and the wisdom of the heart. He says, Know that the Lord alone is God in the heavens above , that is, in the heavens which are above human beings and upon the earth which is under people. And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass [ and the earth that is under thee shall be iron ] (Deut. 28:23) is proof that this interpretation is correct. Now that you have seen the terrors, you shall place in your heart the conviction that you are obligated to observe God’s commandments. The observance of God’s precepts will also go well with you and with your children after you.
THEN MOSES SEPARATED. This means, on the day that Moses separated these cities, he spoke the words of the covenant.
BEYOND THE JORDAN, IN THE VALLEY. The reference is to Mount Abarim before Israel journeyed to the plains of Moab, even though Mount Abarim is in the land of Moab.
AND MOSES CALLED UNTO ALL ISRAEL. As I have explained, to make the children hear the words of the covenant.
IN HOREB. This is Sinai.
THE LORD MADE NOT THIS COVENANT WITH OUR FATHERS. Alone.

BUT WITH US, EVEN US. The meaning of ittanu (even us) is, but also with us. It is similar to thy name shall not be called any more Jacob (Gen. 35:10). Or it means the Lord did not make a covenant with our fathers who were in Egypt but only with us, for there were many in the camp who heard the covenant from the mouth of God. Moses therefore said even us, those who are here, and are alive. Moses’ words, with you (v. 4) and [ I stood ] between [ the Lord ] and you (v. 5) is proof of the correctness of this interpretation.

FACE TO FACE. Without an intermediary. This means I spoke to you, although you did not see Me. The metaphor used in our verse is that of a person who speaks to another person face to face even though the person being spoken to does not see that speaker.
I STOOD BETWEEN THE LORD AND YOU. I have already explained this.
FOR YE WERE AFRAID BECAUSE OF THE FIRE. Even though you did not go up the mountain.

[SAYING.] The word saying is connected to the previous verse. Its meaning is, The Lord spoke with you face to face…out of the midst of the fire (v. 4) saying . It is possible that I stood between the Lord and you means I stood between the Lord and you after the revelation at Sinai. Its meaning is, God spoke with you face to face [at Sinai] and from that day on I stood between the Lord and you because you were afraid, as Moses goes on to explain.

AND WENT NOT UP INTO THE MOUNT. When I went up. Compare, but Moses drew near unto the thick darkness (Ex. 20:18). Do not pay attention to the fact that the word saying is far removed [from the end of verse 4], for there are many such instances. The speaker did not separate the verses and sections. Also do not pay attention to the words, for they are like bodies and their meanings are like souls. One who cuts with two similar tools produces the same result. Scripture therefore interchanges shav (false) (v. 17) and sheker (false) (Ex. 20:13), as these terms are brothers. All lies are vanity. I have already explained that the word zakhor (remember) (v. 8) means the same as shamor (keep). Moses adds, as the Lord thy God commanded thee (v. 12). It means, when you stood around Mount Sinai.
NOR THINE OX, NOR THINE ASS, NOR ANY OF THY CATTLE. A particular followed by a general term. At first only the general term is used. Both say the same.

THAT…MAY REST. Scripture here adds the explanation of the law regarding the man-servant and the maid-servant, namely, And thou shalt remember that thou was a servant . Now God gave rest to your servant. Therefore the Lord your God commanded [thee] to do this on the Sabbath day refers to giving rest to one’s servant. Some say that a servant does not rest. Now God took you out of slavery and commanded you to rest so that you will remember that you were a slave. In the commandment that begins with the word Honor (v. 16), Scripture goes on to say, as the Lord thy God commanded thee . This is to be understood in line with my interpretation.
AND THAT IT MAY GO WELL WITH THEE. Some say that this alludes to the world to come. I will allude to the secret of the world to come in my comments on I kill, and I make alive (Deut. 32:39).

THY DAYS. Scripture goes on to explain that they will be good days. Know that all the early sages are of the opinion that I am (v. 6) is the first statement even though there is room to ask why the one who separated the statements did not separate Thou shalt have no other gods (v. 7). I have already explained the Ten Statements, relying on their opinion. However, I believe that the statement I am is not part of the Ten Statements, for the meaning of I am is, I am the one who commands. I am is the basis of the commandments, as I have explained previously.

The word chamad (coveted) has two meanings in Hebrew. One is to rob, to extort, to take someone’s property by force and compulsion. This is the meaning of the word in neither shall any man covet (yachmod) thy land (Ex. 34:24). For if this is not its meaning, then the land is bad. But Scripture only comes to praise the land. The second meeting is to desire in the heart without acting. Now, Neither shalt thou covet thy neighbor’s house (Ex. 20:14) is the ninth statement, and thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife ( Ibid. ) is the tenth statement. According to this interpretation, thy neighbor’s house and thy neighbor’s wife are connected to each other. On the other hand, thy neighbor’s house might be a general rule. The fact that Moses in this book [Deuteronomy] in which he explains the Torah, employs ve-lo titavveh (neither shalt thou covet) (v. 18) in place of lo tachmod (thou shalt not covet) (Ex. 20:14) is proof of this. Many say that one cannot sin with one’s thoughts and there is no reward and punishment for what one thinks. However, one can refute them by quoting many verses. I will not prolong my argument. I will merely point to the following: A heart that deviseth wicked thoughts (Prov. 6:18); thou didst well that it was in thy heart (II Chron. 6:8); And to them that are upright in their hearts (Ps. 125:4). Moses at the end said, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it (Deut. 30:14). The main purpose of the mitzvot is to perfect the heart. Most of them serve as a memorial. The distinction made between a sin committed deliberately and one committed inadvertently should convince them.
THESE WORDS. Its meaning is, these Ten Statements and not the words which follow them.
A GREAT VOICE. They never heard one like it.
AND IT WENT ON NO MORE. This occurred only one time. Observe, Scripture explains why the voice went on no more , namely, And it came to pass, when ye heard… (v. 20).
HIS GLORY. The appearance of fire.
AND HIS GREATNESS. The voices, the lightning, and the sound of the shofar .
AND…HIS VOICE. The Ten Statements. There is one opinion that God only uttered I am (v. 6).
THE VOICE OF THE LIVING GOD. Elohim (God), as I have explained, is in the plural.
I believe that Scripture uses the term living to differentiate between God and the heavenly host, for the heavenly host does not move by its own power.
AND THOU SHALT SPEAK UNTO US ALL. The word at (thou) is similar to the word at (thou) in And if Thou (at) deal thus with me (Num. 11:15). It is explained there.
THEY HAVE WELL SAID. Hetivu (they have well) is a verb in the perfect. It comes from a root in which only two letters are sounded.

OH THAT. Scripture does not say mi yitten li (oh that I) but rather mi yitten la-hem (oh that they). The word la-hem (they) thus follows ve-hayah levavam zeh (such a heart as this). Note, God’s decrees are the source of all actions and movements. The power and nature of all that is found beneath the heavens is determined by the arrangement of the heavenly bodies. These are connected to the roots below. The same applies to the compounds. All things similarly depend on the movements of the heavenly bodies day by day and time by time, for there is always a change, as the author of the Sefer Yetizrah explained. The parts receive from the categories according to their nature. It is due to the power of the “categories” that they can make some small changes in nature. This is the meaning of and the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart (Ex. 11:10). In another place, Scripture states, and hardened his heart, he and his servants (Ex. 9:34). It is all true. Scripture therefore states, O Lord, I know that man’s way is not his own (Jer. 10:23). It similarly states, O Lord, why dost Thou make us to err from Thy ways (Jer. 63:17). Moses said, therefore choose life (Deut. 30:19). Now, since God does not withhold good, He loves to do good. Scripture employs human language when it says, Oh that .
GO SAY TO THEM. Moses was to go down.

STAND THOU HERE BY ME. Moses was to return. Scripture similarly states, and I will speak unto thee all the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances . It is thus clear that most of the Torah was told to Moses at Sinai. However, Moses transmitted it in the wilderness of Sinai. I believe that he did so in the eleven days that they traveled from Sinai.
YE SHALL OBSERVE TO DO. Scripture states this in order to add, and ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left .

IN ALL THE WAY. This explains to the right hand or to the left . The main purpose of this commandment and the statutes and ordinances is that you, your son, and your son’s son fear the Lord. Faith of the heart is the basis of the commandments. When you fear God, you are fulfilling your destiny as a person. Man, as is noted by Koheleth, was created for this very reason. Furthermore, your days will be prolonged with everyone on the land and for the individual, in the world to come.
AND OBSERVE TO DO IT. Behold. I command you to observe that it may be well with you.
A LAND FLOWING WITH MILK AND HONEY. This is connected to to possess it (v. I). Now, it is far from it, or it is missing a bet , as in that was found in the house of the Lord (II Kings 12:11).

HEAR O ISRAEL: THE LORD ( YHVH ) OUR GOD, THE LORD ( YHVH ) IS ONE.] That which the ancients, of blessed memory, transmitted regarding the reading of the shema is true, and there is no need for further investigation. Note that the glorious name ( YHVH ) is a noun. This being the case, why is it said a second time? The answer is that Adam is a noun. Adam is also an adjective, and not a noun, even though he was called after the very earth. The same is true of the name YHVH . The fact that YHVH is connected to tzeva’ot (hosts) is proof. On the other hand, the term Elohenu (our God) might be the object. The name YHVH was repeated in order to state YHVH echad (the Lord is one) the meaning of which is, only YHVH . There are many proofs that YHVH alone is God. The verse that states, In that day shall the Lord be One (echad) (Zech. 14:9), speaks of men’s thoughts. In my opinion, the word one is connected to the word king, for Scripture writes: And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; In that day shall the Lord alone be King and His name one (Zech. 14:9). The latter is similar in meaning to For then will I turn to the peoples, A pure language, That they may all call upon the name of the Lord (Zeph. 3:9}. Behold, all the nations will speak one language. The name of the Lord will therefore be one.
AND THOU SHALT LOVE. Since we have no other god aside from the Lord, you are obligated to love Him, for we have no other god.

WITH ALL THY HEART, AND WITH ALL THY SOUL. The heart refers to knowledge. It is another term for the spirit of intelligence, for the heart is its first residence. The same applies to wise-hearted (Ex. 36:1) and to He that getteth a heart (Prov. 19:8).
THY SOUL. The reference is to the spirit, which is in the body. It is the spirit which lusts. Its power is manifest in the liver.

THY MIGHT. The meaning of me’odekha (thy might) is very very much. It means that you should love Him to the utmost in any way that you are able. Your heart should be totally committed to the love of God.

AND THESE WORDS…SHALL BE. Those who deny the Rabbinic tradition say that the reference is to the Decalogue, and that it is in reference to the Decalogue that Scripture states, And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts (v. 9). However, the truth is that and these words…shall be refers to all of the commandments.

AND THOU SHALT TEACH THEM. Ve-shinantam (and thou shalt teach them) is related to the word shanun (sharp) in and a sharp arrow (Prov. 25:18). The method of sharpening an arrow is well known. Observe. Our verse teaches that the main purpose of man is to serve God. God’s service consists in recognizing God’s works. However, the transmitters of tradition taught that [our verse] refers to the time of reading the shema . We all rely on them.
WHEN THOU SITTEST. This is connected to and shalt talk of them .
AND WHEN THOU LIEST DOWN. To sleep, for one is not obligated to observe the commandments when one sleeps. Behold, the meaning of our verse is, And thou shalt talk of them verbally and in your heart.
AND THOU SHALT BIND THEM FOR A SIGN UPON THY HAND. This has been explained.

AND THEY SHALL BE FOR FRONTLETS. The word totafot (frontlets) is not found elsewhere in Scripture. Those who dispute the Rabbinic tradition say that totafot is related to the word ve-hatef (and preach) in and preach toward the South (Ezek. 21:2). This is impossible, for the root of hattef is nun, tet, peh . However, there are two tets ands no nun in totafot .
AND THOU SHALT WRITE THEM. They also said that its meaning is Bind them (Prov. 6:8). Now since our fathers received the truth, we will forsake those who employ their heart to invent things.
ALL GOOD THINGS. The word tuv (good) is vocalized with a shuruk in place of a cholam , for these vowels interchange and tuv is not in the construct.
OUT OF THE HOUSE OF BONDAGE. Where you did not possess cities and houses that are full.
THOU SHALT FEAR. You shall not violate any of the negative commandments.
SHALT THOU SERVE. By observing the positive commandments.

AND BY HIS NAME SHALT THOU SWEAR. And not by the name of another god when you affirm anything or make a covenant. Similarly, Every tongue shall swear (Is. 45:23). You shall swear only the truth. The meaning of our verse is, you shall have no other god to swear by his name. You shall only swear by the name of the Lord. Scripture therefore afterwards reads, Ye shall not go after other gods (v. 14), and ye shall not try the Lord your God (v. 16).

IN MASSAH. Massah is the name of a place mentioned earlier, And the name of the place was called Massah (Ex. 17:7). The bet which is prefixed to Massah is vocalized with a pattach like the bet prefixed to karkor in Now Zebah and Zalmona were in Karkor (Jud. 8:10), and the bet placed before Telaim in And numbered them in Telaim (I Sam. 15:4). I explained it there. Massah was so called because Israel said, Is the Lord among us (Ex. 17:7). If He is, then we will serve Him. [Moses told Israel:] you have no need to test God. All you have to do is observe His commandments. If you do what is good in His sight, the Lord will do to you all that is good for you and will thrust out all of your enemies.
TO THRUST OUT. The heh in la-hadof (to thrust out) is a root letter, as the word hadofo (cast it upon him) (Num. 35:22) proves.

WHAT MEAN THE TESTIMONIES. It means, Why, out of all people, is this burden placed upon us? [21.] THEN THOU SHALT SAY. For God redeemed us from the house of bondage. Now, God did us this good. We are obligated to fear His name because we have recognized that He did good to us in the past. He will do good for us in the future to keep us alive, for His commandments are life unto those that find them (Prov. 4:22).

AND IT SHALL BE RIGHTEOUSNESS UNTO US. Some say that this verse hints at the reward in the world to come for the observance of the commandments. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, our verse teaches that following God’s will is the righteous thing to do, for He is our Master. I believe that the correct meaning is, all the nations shall see that we are righteous when we keep God’s commandments and statutes, which Scripture clearly states are righteous.
AND SHALL CAST OUT. The nun in ve-nashal (and shall cast out) is a root letter. It is related to the word yishal (shall drop off) in for thine olives shall drop off (Deut. 28:40).
FOR HE WILL TURN AWAY THY SON. The reference is to “his son” mentioned earlier. That is, do not give your daughter to his son or do not take the daughter mentioned.
BUT THUS. Ki im ko ta’asu la-ham means but thus shall ye deal with them because thou art a holy people (v. 6) and should not defile yourself with pagan images drawn on pillars, or with asherim .

HIS OWN TREASURE. I have already explained the meaning of the word segullah (treasure). It means a desirable thing to which nothing comparable is to be found any-where. Segullat (treasure) in and treasure such as kings…have as their own (Eccles. 2:8) is similar.
SET HIS LOVE UPON YOU, NOR CHOOSE YOU. You and not anyone else.
AND BECAUSE HE WOULD KEEP. U-mi-shomro (and because he would keep) is an infinitive.

HE IS GOD. This means this is truly the God who has the power and is faithful. And is faithful refers to the oath which God took. Scripture says that God is powerful and faithful, because there are others who are faithful but lack the power to keep their oaths and others who are powerful but are unfaithful.
WHO KEEPETH COVENANT AND MERCY WITH THEM THAT LOVE HIM. There are none higher then they.
AND KEEP HIS COMMANDMENTS. After them. Or its meaning is, them that love Him in their hearts, they are the ones who keep His commandments verbally and in practice.

TO A THOUSAND GENERATIONS. The one who says that the sphere of the constellations completes its cycle at the end of thirty-six thousand years errs, for we find it moving one degree in seventy years. The meaning of a thousand is, endless.
AND REPAYETH THEM THAT HATE HIM…TO DESTROY THEM. To destroy each individual that hates Him. Compare, But righteous people is secure as a young lion (Prov. 28:1).

TO THEIR FACE. Be-fanav (to their face) means to him. Others say that el panav (their face) has the meaning of befanav , that is, because of His anger. Its means that God will repay the wicked because they hated the truth.

TO DESTROY THEM; HE WILL NOT BE SLACK TO HIM THAT HATETH HIM. Some say that the meaning of our verse is that God rewards the wicked for his good deeds in this world and does not wait to reward him in the world to come. However, it appears to me that our verse contrasts the righteous who will exist for a thousand generations with the wicked who will be destroyed. Scripture reads, He will not be slack because the wicked person thinks that his son or grandson shall live, as in [ visiting the iniquity of the fathers ] upon the children, and upon the children’s children (Ex. 33:7).
THOU SHALT THEREFORE KEEP. It means as God keeps the covenant so shall you keep His commandments.

BECAUSE. Ekev (because) has the same meaning as ekev (reward) in For ever, reward (Ps. 119:112). It means the reward which will be given at the end. The meaning of who keepeth covenant in the previous verse (v. 9) is that God kept the covenant with Abraham. If you will be among those that love Him, then He will continue to keep the covenant. If you will be among those who love Him, then He will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee (v. 13). This is the meaning of the covenant and the mercy (v. 12).
THY BODY. Thy children. Bitnekha (thy body) is a euphemism.
AND THE FRUIT OF THY LAND. Scripture mentions com, wine, and oil because they are the most important foods.
THE INCREASE. I have already explained the meaning of shegar (the increase of).
THY KINE. The word alafekha (thy kine) is similar to the word alufenu (oxen) in Whose oxen are well laden (Ps. 144:14).

AND THE YOUNG OF. Ashterot (and the young of) means and the flocks of. There was a great commentator in Spain who explained why the Hebrews referred to cattle as alef and to sheep and goats as ashterot . He similarly explained the ba’alim and the ashtaroth (Jud. 10:6) as referring to the lord of the flowering constellation and that of the tenth. Scripture goes on to say God will not only bless the fruit of your body but there will not be a barren male, that is, one whose seed is infertile, among you or among your cattle. Furthermore, you will be healthy and avoid all sorts of well-known illnesses which normally befall people. You will similarly avoid abnormal, evil diseases.
AND THOU SHALT CONSUME. This is a commandment to consume them as one consumes bread, as thine eye shall not pity them proves.
FOR THAT WILL BE A SNARE UNTO THEE. The reference is to each one of their gods.
THE HORNET. Ha-tzirah (the hornet) refers to an illness which afflicts the body. It is related to the word tzara’at (leprosy).
THOU SHALT NOT BE AFFRIGHTED AT THEM. Only fear the Lord, who is great and awful.

LEST THE BEASTS OF THE FIELD INCREASE UPON THEE. The Gaon says that this is a sign regarding the time that they shall be victorious over them. There is no need for the Gaon’s interpretation. I have already explained it.

THOU HAST DESTROYED THEM. Hishmidekha (thou has destroyed them) is an infinitive even though it is vocalized with a chirik . The word hishir (left him remaining) in until there was none left him remaining (Num. 22:35) is most likely similar to it. The word otam (them), which is the object, proves that hishmidekha is an infinitive.
THE SILVER OR THE GOLD THAT IS ON THEM. Alehem is to be rendered, that is on them. Or the meaning of our clause is, you shall not take money to leave them.
SNARED. The vav in tivvakesh (snared) is in place of a yod . Compare, yakoshti lakh (I have laid a snare for thee).
ALL THE COMMANDMENT. This means, if you want to keep the commandments so that you may live then remember all the way (v. 2).
THAT HE MIGHT AFFLICT THEE, TO PROVE THEE. I have already explained it.
AND HE AFFLICTED THEE. On the way.

AND SUFFERED THEE TO HUNGER. Before the coming of the manna. Or via the manna itself, for it was light and did not satisfy their heart’s desire. However, this is not so. It most probably refers to other desires.

KNOW. Yade’un (know) is spelled with a nun . So too the word tzakun (poured out) in Silently they poured out a prayer (Is. 26:16) and va-yachanun (and they pitched) in and they pitched on the other side of the Arnon (Jud. 11:18).
THAT HE MIGHT MAKE THEE KNOW. Hodi’akha (make thee know) is an infinitive.
BREAD. Which people always eat.

EVERY THING THAT PROCEEDETH OUT OF THE MOUTH OF THE LORD. It means that which God has decreed. Compare, As the word went out of the king’s mouth (Esth. 7:8). The meaning of our verse is, man does not live by bread alone but by the power, or with the power, which comes from on high by the command of God. This is the meaning of that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord . The fact that you did not eat bread and you lived is proof of this.
THY RAIMENT. Some say via a miracle. Others say that the Israelites brought out many garments from Egypt. However, it is most likely the nature of manna not to produce sweat.

NEITHER…SWELL. The word batzekah (swell) is related to the word batzek (dough) in And they baked…the dough (Ex. 12:39). It is usual for the feet of a wayfarer who walks great distances to swell. It is possible that God gave the Israelites strength or that he led them slowly.

AND THOU SHALT CONSIDER IN THY HEART. You shall know by believing in your heart. The latter is what counts most. God will reward you by bringing you into the good land, because you obeyed the God who chastens you. You obeyed God even though in order to chasten you, He afflicted you with thirst and made you suffer hunger.
A LAND OF WHEAT. Moses makes mention of the foods which produce blood.
AND HONEY. I have already explained this.
SCARCENESS. Be-miskenut (scarceness) means in poverty and impoverishment. Compare, misken (poor) in a poor and wise child (Eccles. 4:13).
MULTIPLY. The yod in yirbeyun (multiply) is in place of a heh . This is not the opinion of Rabbi Mosheh Ha-Kohen the Spaniard.

THEN THY HEART BE LIFTED UP. And you will forget that you were a slave and your heart was downcast. You will forget the affliction and the hunger which you experienced in the wilderness and even so the Lord sustained you.
WILDERNESS. The word midbar (wilderness) is to be read as if written twice, that is, through the great wilderness in length and width and [through] a dreadful wilderness of fiery serpents.
OF FLINT. Tzur ha-chalamish (the rock of flint) means the mighty rock.
THIS WEALTH. Chayil means wealth. Compare, the word chelam (their wealth) in And leave their wealth to others (Ps. 49:11). Chelam refers to that which they acquired by their efforts and strength.
BUT THOU SHALT REMEMBER. This means if the thought My power and the might of my hand hath gotten me this wealth should enter your mind, then remember the One who gives you power.
BECAUSE. The word ekev (because) refers to payment at the end. It refers both to reward and to punishment.
THOU ART TO PASS OVER THE JORDAN THIS DAY. At this time. Or it means, imagine that you are passing over today.
AS A DEVOURING FIRE. Quickly. Scripture therefore goes on to say quickly .
The lamed prefixed to le-min (from) in le-min ha-yom (from the day) is superfluous. There are many such instances.
IN THE WILDERNESS. After they journeyed from Horeb.
FINGER. This has already been explained.
AT THE END. At the end or the beginning of the fortieth day. Look. This verse shows that the golden calf was made on the day that the tablets were given to Moses.
AND I FELL DOWN. The reference is to Moses’ statement, and now I will go up unto the Lord (Ex. 32:30).
The meaning of and now I fell down is, I fell with my face to the ground.

THAT TIME ALSO. For he had previously prayed for Israel when they were at the sea. Wherefore criest thou unto me (Ex. 14:15) is proof of the latter. Furthermore, Scripture states, and he cried unto the Lord; and the Lord showed him a tree (Ex. 15:25).
AND I TOOK YOUR SIN. The calf is referred to by the term sin. Hence Moses goes on to explain and says, the calf .
AND BEAT IT. Into fine dust like the dust of the ground.

AND AT TABERAH. Taberah is probably the name of a place. Israel camped there for but one day. Therefore Scripture does not mention it in the Torah portion Elleh Mase (These Are the Stages) (Num. 33:1). It is one of the thirty journeys that Israel traveled from Mount Sinai until they came to Kibroth-hattaavah (Num. 33:17), as I explained. The reason Scripture connects Taberah with Massah is that the people were as murmurers (Num. 11:1); that is, they tested God. Scripture mentions Taberah before Massah because nothing happened to Israel at Massah. Some say that Amalek came because Israel tested God. Scripture therefore mentions the burning of God’s fire among them, Amalek’s smiting of Israel’s hindmost, and the smiting of those who lusted. Scripture mentions the most severe punishments first. Some say that Taberah and Massah are one and the same place. It is like From the top of Senir and Hermon (Cant. 4:8). However, my interpretation is correct.
YE BELIEVED HIM NOT. In your hearts.
NOR HEARKENED. In deed. Moses then goes back to describe the prayer which he offered.
THY PEOPLE AND THINE INHERITANCE. Because of their fathers.
The meaning of Thy people is, it is well known that they are thy people, for You took them out by Your great power, which You demonstrated to the world.
AT THAT TIME. During the forty days that are mentioned.

AN ARK OF WOOD. The transmitters of tradition, of blessed memory, said that Moses first made another ark. Proof of the latter is, So I made an ark (v. 3), which is followed by and hewed two tables of stone (v. 3) and put the tables in the ark which I had made (v. 5). Now their minds are superior to our minds, for it appears to us that And the glory of the Lord abode (Ex. 24:16) is connected with the glory which the elders saw (Ex. 24:10). We do not know when Moses ascended, for according to the plain meaning of the text it appears that Moses fasted for only eighty days, for the meaning of Now I stayed in the mount (v. 10) repeats what was said earlier. It means when I stayed on the mountain during those forty days God listened to me and said, Arise, go before the people (v. 11), the reference being to And now go, lead the people (Ex. 32:34). The making of the ark of wood (v. 3) was thus by command. It refers to the ark made by Bezalel.

SO I MADE AN ARK. By command. The meaning of And Moses assembled (Ex. 35:1) should be interpreted, and Moses had assembled. I have already shown you many such instances. All of this is necessitated by Scripture’s statement, and there they are, as the Lord commanded me (v. 5). This is what And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony (Ex. 25:16) refers to. It is also possible that it refers to and make thee an ark of wood . The tradition of the sages shall triumph.

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL JOURNEYED FROM BEEROTH-BENEJAAKAN TO MOSERAH; THERE AARON DIED. This verse is placed here because Moses said, And I prayed for Aaron also the same time (Deut. 9:20). Moses indicated that Aaron did not die until the fortieth year (Num. 33:38). Moses’ statement, At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi (v. 8), which took place at Mount Sinai as I explained in the Torah portion which opens with And The Lord Spoke (Num. 1:1), is proof that this is its meaning. The early authorities tell us that Israel backtracked. However, what shall we do with the clause, there Aaron died, and there he was buried ? Rabbi Isaac ibn Giat the Spaniard, of blessed memory, says that the meaning of sham (there) is then. He says that mi-sham (from thence) in misham ro’eh (from thence, from the shepherd) (Gen. 49:24) is similar. There is no need for this interpretation. On the contrary, I believe that Beeroth-benejaakan is not to be identified with Bene-jaakkan; neither is Moserah the same as Moserot (Num. 33:31). In reality Kadesh is called the wilderness of Beeroth-benejaakan, and the wilderness of Mount Hor is called Moserah. There are many such examples. Do you not see that Scripture says the wilderness of Shur (Ex. 15:22)? However, in another place Scripture refers to it as the wilderness of Etam (Num. 33:18).

FROM THENCE THEY JOURNEYED UNTO GUDGOD. The latter is not to be identified with Hor-haggidgad (Num. 33:32). On the contrary, it is a general term for Zalmonah and also for Punon and Oboth (Num. 33:43,44).

[TO JOTBAH.] Jotbah is the place that is also called Beer, for Scripture reads, And from thence to Beer (Num. 21:16). This is what a land of brooks of water (v. 7) refers to, for the nobles of the people dug it with their staves and water came forth (Num. 21:18). This verse, namely, From thence they journeyed unto Gudgod is connected to and Eleazar…ministered (v. 6). Now, I have already explained to you that Israel did not offer sacrifices after they journeyed from Mount Sinai. It is possible that they offered them when they came to Zalmonah and Punon and that the beginning of Eleazar’s service as high priest started in those places on Rosh Ha-Shanah. He ministered in a place called Beer on Yom Kippur. The meaning of our verses thus is, And Eleazar ministered when they came to such and such a place. Why did Eleazar minister? Because when Israel worshipped the calf, God separated the tribe of Levi to carry the ark and to stand before the Lord.
TO MINISTER UNTO HIM. The sons of Levi with the sons of Aaron.
AND TO BLESS IN HIS NAME. For Eleazar lifted up his hands.
THE LORD IS HIS INHERITANCE. Its meaning is the same as O Lord, the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup (Ps. 16:5). It refers to serving God by learning His ways.
NOW I STAYED IN THE MOUNT. I have already explained this.
CAUSING THEM TO SET FORWARD. Massa (causing to set forward) is an infinitive.
AND HE CHOSE THEIR SEED. Their seed being you. This is the meaning of even you .

CIRCUMCISE THEREFORE THE FORESKIN OF YOUR HEART. The reference is to separation from lusts, which are as gross and leaden as a foreskin. It is also possible that it refers to cleansing the heart until one understands the truth.
STIFFNECKED. I have already explained the meaning of this term. Furthermore, he earlier said, for thou art a stiffnecked people (Deut. 9:6).
GOD OF GODS. I have already explained this.
LORD OF LORDS. For they are on various high levels, as in and there are higher than they (Eccles. 8:7). The one who knows these measures is of circumcised heart.

HE DOTH EXECUTE JUSTICE. Even though He is exalted, He executes justice on behalf of the orphan and widow who have no one to help them, as in a father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows (Ps. 68:6). He similarly loves the stranger and sustains him when he relies on Him. Now, since God loves the stranger, you too are obligated to love him.
THOU SHALT FEAR THE LORD THY GOD. You shall not violate the negative commandments.
HIM SHALT THOU SERVE. By observing the positive commandments.
AND TO HIM SHALT THOU CLEAVE. With your heart.
AND BY HIS NAME SHALT THOU SWEAR. With your mouth as Scripture explains.
HE IS THY GLORY. Its meaning is, you should glorify yourself in Him, for He did these tremendous things for you.
WITH THREE SCORE AND TEN. I have already explained this.
THEREFORE THOU SHALT LOVE THE LORD. Since the Lord multiplied you, you are obligated to love Him. Our verse adds always .

I SPEAK NOT WITH YOUR CHILDREN THAT HAVE NOT KNOWN. The answer is, but your eyes have seen (v. 7). It means these wonders are not future phenomena which your children shall see. On the contrary, you yourselves have witnessed them.
HIS GREATNESS, HIS MIGHTY HAND, AND HIS OUTSTRETCHED ARM. In taking you out of Egypt.
AND HIS SIGNS, AND HIS WORKS. Unto Pharaoh , for he was most important.
HE MADE…TO OVERFLOW. The word hetzif (made to overflow) is related to the word tzafu (flowed) in Waters flowed over my head (Lam. 3:54).
DESTROYED THEM. Its meaning is, their children did not arise in their place to be like them.
AND WHAT HE DID UNTO YOU IN THE WILDERNESS. The reference is to the manna.
AND THEIR HOUSEHOLDS. The reference is to their wives and to their children.
AND EVERY LIVING SUBSTANCE. Yekum (substance) is an all-inclusive term.

THAT FOLLOWED THEM. Be-raglehem (that followed them) means because of them. On the other hand, the term may be taken literally. Since you have seen all of this, take heed so that you observe God’s commandments.
AND POSSESS. The resh in vi-yerishtem (and possess) is vocalized with a chirik because the vav is vocalized with a chirik .

FOR THE LAND. Here is another reason why you are obligated to observe God’s commandments. The land is not like the land of Egypt. On the contrary, the land needs God to keep His eye on it. The meaning of our verse can be understood with the following parable. The Lord will act like a person who sees all that the land needs and will give everything in its time.

FROM THE BEGINNING. Me-reshit (from the beginning) is spelled without an alef . There are many such instances. Scripture therefore goes on to say, And it shall come to pass (v. 13); and I will give the rain of your land in its season (v. 14). This is what Scripture means by the eyes of the Lord are always upon it .
THE FORMER RAIN. The word yoreh (former rain) refers to rain which indicates a good year. It comes at the beginning of the year.
AND THE LATTER RAIN. The meaning of malkosh (the latter rain) is known.
AND THOU SHALT EAT AND BE SATISFIED. This refers to thy corn, and thy wine (v. 14), not to that which comes immediately before it namely, grass in thy fields .
HER FRUIT. I have previously explained the meaning of yevulah (her fruit).
AND YE PERISH QUICKLY. They will be exiled from the land like those who perish in hunger. Now, since the land is good, you are therefore obligated to take these words to heart.

FOR FRONTLETS. Its meaning has been explained. If you will take My words to heart, you will not be exiled from the land, and your days upon the land shall be as long as the days of the heaven above the earth.

FOR IF YE SHALL DILIGENTLY KEEP. The meaning of our verse is: I told you that you will quickly be driven from the good land. Know that you will not initially enter the land, and you will not be victorious if you do not keep the commandments of God.
TO LOVE. With your heart.
TO WALK IN ALL HIS WAYS. Not to change or overturn.
AND TO CLEAVE UNTO HIM. Ultimately. This is a great secret.
BEHOLD. Moses speaks to each individual.

THE BLESSING, IF YE SHALL HEARKEN. For if you hearken, behold, you are blessed. A blessing means an addition of the good. A curse means a diminution. The word kelalah (curse) is related to the word kallah (light).
THAT THOU SHALT SET THE BLESSING. Verbally, as in and he shall put them upon the head of the goat (Lev. 16:21).
BEYOND THE JORDAN. To one standing on the side of the wilderness.
BEHIND THE WAY OF THE GOING DOWN OF THE SUN. This means when you follow the western road you will find them.
IN THE LAND OF THE CANAANITES THAT DWELL IN THE ARABAH. For there are Canaanites who dwell in the mountain.

OVER AGAINST GILGAL. The mountains are long. Look. Moses specified the place by command. Over against Gilgal is similar to and pursued as far as Dan (Gen. 14:14). It is possible that it was prophetically stated, or we are dealing with two names.
OVER AGAINST. The word mul means over against.
BESIDE THE TEREBINTHS OF MOREH. This is the same place as mentioned in the days of Abraham. Scripture will later on state the blessings and the curses.
FOR YE ARE TO PASS OVER. This means, thus shall you commence to do and the land will be yours eternally for an inheritance.

YE SHALL SURELY DESTROY ALL THE PLACES…THEIR GODS. Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that et elohehem (their gods) is lacking a vav , for the meaning of the phrase is, and their gods. However, he contributes nothing. Et elohehem is most certainly connected to asher avedu sham (wherein they served).
EVERY LEAFY TREE. The words ra’anan (leafy) and sha’anan (at peace) are always spelled with two nuns . The meaning of ra’anan is wet.
THEIR ASHERIM. Asherim are trees.
AND YE SHALL DESTROY THEIR NAME. So that they not be mentioned.
YE SHALL NOT DO SO. This means do not sacrifice on the hills and the mountains. Do so only in the place where the Lord shall put His name.
TO PUT HIS NAME THERE. Compare, Where I cause My name to be mentioned (Ex. 20:21).
EVEN UNTO HIS HABITATIONS SHALL YE SEEK. The reference is to the land, that is, to the place where God’s glory dwells.
AND THERE YE SHALL EAT. The kohanim and the Levites.

YE SHALL NOT DO AFTER ALL THAT WE DO HERE THIS DAY. Scripture states this because they were journeying from station to station. After Aaron’s death some would sacrifice a burnt offering in any one of the stations that he desired to do so. Some would present the first-born of the flock. Others did not, for the commandment is contingent upon the Land of Israel. However, this is not my opinion. Its meaning, rather, is that not all of them feared God. Now, Moses said “we” because, as Scripture clearly states, he made the many commandments regarding the burnt offering contingent upon the Land of Israel.

TO THE REST. So that they and their children do not have to travel. This is the meaning of inheritance. However, actually the meaning of the rest is, and giveth you rest (v. 10), and the inheritance refers to so that ye dwell in safety (v. 10).
AND ALL YOUR CHOICE VOWS. The commandment requires that offerings made by vows be brought from the choicest.
Behold, another addition, namely, And ye shall rejoice (v. 12). AND THE LEVITE. You are obligated to make the Levite happy, for he does not have an inheritance as you do.

Scripture repeats in every place that thou seest (v. 13) because it wants to exclude meat eaten out of desire. Scripture states the unclean and the clean (v. 15) with regard to meat eaten out of desire because peace offerings are sacred and one who eats sacred meat in a state of impurity incurs the penalty of excision.

AS OF THE GAZELLE, AND AS OF THE HART. Which are not offered on the altar. The fat of the gazelle and also that of the hart, is permitted. Look, this is proof of my words. However, we rely on the tradition of our fathers.
THOU MAYEST NOT EAT WITHIN THY GATES THE TITHE OF THY CORN. Moses speaks to the Levites. According to many he also speaks to the Israelites regarding the second tithe.

OR THE FIRSTLINGS OF THY HERD OR OF THY FLOCK. Moses speaks to the kohanim , for the Levites and also the kohanim are included among the Israelites. Compare, And I commanded you (Deut. 3:18) wherein Moses speaks to two and a half tribes. Similarly, Moses speaks to Israel when he says, the first-born of man shalt thou surely redeem (Num. 18:15), which means the one who is obligated to redeem. Similarly, Thou mayest not eat within thy gates and but thou shalt eat them before the Lord thy God (v. 18) refer to the one who is obligated to eat. The heretics say that there are two sorts of first-born. One is the first to break out of its mother’s womb. The second is the first-born of the flock. There is no need to respond to their nonsense. There are also others who say that if an Israelite is in the chosen place, then he eats the first-born and the tithe. However, this is the reverse of what Scripture says.

BECAUSE THY SOUL DESIRETH TO EAT FLESH. This means, if your soul desires to eat flesh. Moses already mentioned this. He repeats himself in order to add, If the place…be too far from thee (v. 21). Furthermore, this verse speaks of a place that is not part of the land of Canaan. Its law is the same as the law within your gates.
FOR THE BLOOD IS THE LIFE. I have explained this previously.

THAT IT MAY GO WELL WITH THEE. A person should not eat the soul [blood] of an animal for it will harm his soul. Also, one’s soul and form are in the image of the father. Scripture therefore states, and with thy children after thee .
ONLY THY HOLY THINGS. Burnt offerings, peace offerings, and vow offerings.
THOU SHALT TAKE. This means bring them to the chosen place.

AND THOU SHALT EAT THE FLESH. Moses speaks to the kohen concerning a first-born, a sin offering, a guilt offering, or the shoulder or breast. If the kohen eats from a peace offering, the major part belongs to the Israelite.
OBSERVE AND HEAR. Observe and hear means, observe and hear the law regarding the blood which is to be poured on the altar.
WHEN THE LORD…SHALL CUT OFF. This section also is connected to When the Lord…shall enlarge thy border (v. 20), for if Israel does not conquer the nations, God will not enlarge Israel’s border.
AND THAT…NOT.] U-fen (and that…not) introduces an abridged clause. So that you will follow their practices [has been omitted].

EVEN SO WILL I DO LIKEWISE. In the service of the Lord, and you will think that you are doing good. You shall not act in this manner, for God despises all their ways. For even their sons…do they burn in the fire to their gods is proof of the latter. That which I commanded you, that shall you observe to do.

IF THERE ARISE IN THE MIDST OF THEE. Scripture reads in the midst of thee because there is no prophet except from among Israel. This section is connected to the previous one because they both deal with idol worship, for the burning of the children (Deut. 12:31) was an act of idol worship. Our verse deals with a prophet who claims that God, or God’s messenger, spoke to him while he was awake or in a dream. Some say that it is possible that the prophet was one of those who steal God’s word (Jer. 26:30). They explain that a true prophet said that a certain sign would appear to verify his word. Someone heard this and related the sign so that it should bear witness for him. Others say that even if the sign or a wonder came to pass we do not believe him, for what he says contradicts reason. I believe that the terms wonder and sign apply also to symbolic acts. Compare, the words of the prophet Isaiah: Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me shall be for signs and for wonders (Is. 8:18); the sign of the prophet in Like as My servant Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot (Is. 20:3); the names of his children, which served as signs regarding things that would occur in their lifetime, namely, Emanuel (Is. 7:14); Maher-shalal-hash-baz (Is. 8:3); Shearjashub (Is. 7:3). Also Scripture’s statement with regard to the plagues, And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder (Deut. 28:46). There are many such instances.

[PUTTETH YOU TO PROOF.] Scripture says, for the Lord…putteth you to proof , because God left the prophet alone and did not kill him. The purpose of God’s test is to show the righteousness of the one who is being tried.
AFTER THE LORD YOUR GOD SHALL YE WALK. You shall do your utmost to imitate God’s deeds and pursue His paths.
AND HIM SHALL YE FEAR. You shall refrain from asking why this is so.
AND HIS COMMANDMENTS SHALL YE KEEP. The commandments which are most important.
AND UNTO HIS VOICE SHALL YE HEARKEN. This refers to precepts which recall that which is most important.
AND HIM SHALL YE SERVE. In deed.
AND UNTO HIM SHALL YE CLEAVE. With your heart. In the beginning and at the end.
BECAUSE HE HATH SPOKEN PERVERSION. The word davar (thing) has been omitted from our clause. But in the multitude of counselors established (Prov. 15:22) is similar.

Scripture reads sarah (perversion) because God commanded Israel to turn away ( la-sur ) from idolatry. On the other hand, the word sarah might be related to the word soreh (defiant) in defiant and rebellious (Deut. 21:20). The latter interpretation is correct. The resh should have received a dagesh .
WHO BROUGHT YOU OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT, AND REDEEMED THEE OUT OF THE HOUSE OF BONDAGE. Scripture repeats itself for the sake of emphasis.
SO SHALT THOU PUT AWAY. I have previously explained the meaning of u-vi’arta (so thou put away).
IF THY BROTHER…ENTICE THEE. This means even thy brother.
The import of thy mother is, you were in one womb. The mother is like matter and the father is like form. Very few people understand the nature of form.
THOU SHALT NOT CONSENT UNTO HIM. By believing in your heart.
NOR HEARKEN UNTO HIM. In deed.
NEITHER SHALL THINE EYE PITY HIM. You shall not refrain from killing him.
NEITHER SHALT THOU CONCEAL HIM. You shall not leave him alone but you shall reveal the matter until witnesses hear it from his mouth, as is stated in Scripture. You shall then kill him.
THY HAND SHALL BE FIRST UPON HIM. Were it not for tradition, it would appear that the reference is to the two witnesses.
AND THOU SHALT STONE HIM. Scripture explains the manner of his death.
THEN SHALT THOU INQUIRE, AND MAKE SEARCH, AND ASK DILIGENTLY. These words are well explained in the writings of our rabbis of blessed memory.
EVERY WHIT. Completely to the Lord your God. You shall bum it in fire because of God’s honor.
A HEAP. The word tel (heap) is related to talul (heaped) in upon a high mountain and heaped (Ezek. 17:22).
THAT THE LORD MAY TURN FROM THE FIERCENESS OF HIS ANGER. And He will not destroy you because of the sins of that city.

WHEN THOU SHALT HEARKEN. The meaning of When thou shalt hearken is, thus shall you do if you desire to do what is right in the eyes of God. The section which opens with Ye are children of the Lord (Deut. 14:1) is connected to this section because of the enticers, namely, a brother, a sister, and a son or daughter (v. 7), or the inhabitants of the idol-worshipping city (v. 14). It is prohibited to mourn for them, and it is certainly prohibited to cut oneself, for behold, that is prohibited over any deceased.
